ch02.goal.slope: The slope of $x(t)$ is the instantaneous velocity $v$; the slope of $v(t)$ is the acceleration $a$
ch02.goal.area: The area under $a(t)$ is the change in velocity $\Delta v$; the area under $v(t)$ is the displacement $\Delta x$
ch02.obs.slope: Derivative relation: compare the slope of the tangent to $x(t)$ with the height of the dot on $v(t)$
ch02.obs.area: Integral relation: area where $v < 0$ is negative (hatched), so $x$ decreases
ch02.obs.turn: Turnaround: when $v = 0$ the tangent to $x(t)$ is horizontal and the object reverses
ch02.obs.custom: Custom: drag the bars on the $a(t)$ graph up or down to set each segment's acceleration
ch02.assume: Acceleration is constant within each segment
ch02.d.motion: How the acceleration changes over time
ch02.d.mode: Derivative: a slope gives the next graph's value. Integral: an area gives the change in the previous graph
ch02.d.v0: Velocity at $t = 0$ for the custom motion
ch02.d.vectors: Show velocity and acceleration arrows on the object
ch02.ff.d.throw: Initial velocity: 0, 10 m/s up, or 10 m/s down
ch02.ff.d.h: Height where the ball is released
ch02.ff.d.strobe: Mark the ball's position every 0.1 s
ch02.ff.goal.const: Free fall is motion with constant acceleration $a = -g$ ($g = 9.8$ m/s²)
ch02.ff.goal.up: Thrown upward, the acceleration is still $-g$ the whole time, including at the top
ch02.ff.obs.graphs: $a(t)$ is flat, $v(t)$ is a line of slope $-g$, $y(t)$ is a parabola
ch02.ff.obs.top: Throw up: at the top $v = 0$ while $a = -g$
ch02.ff.obs.strobe: Drop with strobe: distances fallen in equal time intervals go as 1 : 3 : 5 : …
ch02.ff.obs.area: Integral relation: the area $-gt$ under $a(t)$ is the change in velocity $\Delta v$
